solutionSql:
CREATE TABLE rate_card (
  id integer PRIMARY KEY,
  carrier_code text NOT NULL,
  lane text NOT NULL,
  rate_per_kg numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (rate_per_kg > 0),
  UNIQUE (carrier_code, lane)
);

sampleChecks.Columns of rate_card: id integer, carrier_code text, lane text (all NOT NULL), rate_per_kg numeric(12,2) NOT NULL.
sampleChecks.Constraints on rate_card: PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE (carrier_code, lane), CHECK (rate_per_kg > 0), NOT NULL on all four columns.

constraintProbes.repeated lane rejected: Second DHL / LANE1 row failed with 23505 (rate_card_carrier_code_lane_key). Matches expected 23505.
constraintProbes.valid rate accepted: Rate 4.25 inserted without error. Matches expected ok.

ambiguities.phrase: a numeric value with two decimal places
ambiguities.readingChosen: numeric(12,2), matching the invoice amount column type.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Another total precision with scale 2, such as numeric(10,2). Values are the same for practical amounts, but a column-type check may compare precision.

notes: The behaviour of all three probes matches the test names. Only the declared precision is open, so a strict column-type check could go either way.
